headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: Replit Agent’s broad shell/network/file access can expose secrets and mutate shared Repl state, while godot_rl_agents provides no compensating controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between godot_rl_agents and Replit Agent, so prompt injection is not default. However, Replit Agent can read/write Repl files and act inside the workspace, so if the pair is manually bridged through copied files or prompts, attacker-controlled content could influence it. The pathway is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies godot_rl_agents output into a Replit workspace file or prompt, THEN Replit Agent can ingest it as instructions.
IF a shared file or pasted transcript is used as the bridge, THEN prompt injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste model outputs into executable prompts.
Use a plain-text handoff template with explicit delimiters.
Review copied content before Replit Agent reads it.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for handoff files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly touches secrets, source code, and deployment configuration and has broad network egress plus filesystem access. godot_rl_agents is docs-only and shows no data-touching surfaces, so the main leakage risk is one-way from Replit Agent when shared files or secrets are present. The pair can expose sensitive workspace data if the Repl contains it.
conditions: IF the Repl workspace contains secrets or deployment configuration, THEN Replit Agent can read and transmit them.
IF the operator places sensitive files into the shared Repl workspace, THEN leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace before running Replit Agent.
Store credentials only in the secrets manager.
Limit the Repl to non-sensitive sample data.
Check outbound requests after each run.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace secret scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad shell/network capabilities in a persistent Repl filesystem. godot_rl_agents is not shown to coordinate or lock shared state, so if both are used on the same repo or Repl, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state. The default Replit persistence makes this dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same Repl filesystem or git repository, THEN write conflicts can occur.
IF Replit Agent commits or rewrites files while godot_rl_agents also produces artifacts, THEN state corruption or lost work can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate repo or branch.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use manual diff review before commits.
Back up the workspace before edits.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Replit Agent can act on workspace files and shell commands, so if it consumes outputs from godot_rl_agents as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or deployment actions. godot_rl_agents is a game-playing repo with no documented verification layer, so the pair lacks an explicit cross-check. The blast radius is multiple work products rather than immediate irreversible harm.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents output is copied into Replit Agent as facts or instructions, THEN Replit Agent may act on it without verification.
IF Replit Agent uses those outputs to edit code or deployment files, THEN downstream errors propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before actions.
Separate analysis from execution steps.
Ask Replit Agent to cite source files before acting.
Use a checklist for any generated changes.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl, which can create residency or retention concerns. godot_rl_agents is open-source and docs-only, so it does not add a separate compliance burden, but the pair still inherits Replit-side handling of sensitive data. The risk is policy mismatch rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the Repl workspace, THEN Replit Agent’s cloud handling may conflict with local policy.
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the workspace contents, THEN the pair may violate them.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the Repl.
Confirm residency requirements before upload.
Use synthetic or redacted inputs.
Review retention settings in Replit.
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA or approved hosting configuration.
